stem: When teaching breast health maintenance after transplantation, which self-care practice aligns with standard references?

options.text: Breast self-examination only once every ten years
No breast self-examination because immunosuppression prevents breast cancer
Breast self-examination is discouraged for transplant recipients

explanation.rationale_correct: Breast health teaching includes monthly self-examination along with mammograms per provider assessment or American Cancer Society recommendations.

rationale_incorrect.B: Standard references recommend monthly rather than decennial self-examination.
rationale_incorrect.C: Immunosuppression increases malignancy risk; breast self-examination remains recommended.
rationale_incorrect.D: Monthly breast self-examination is part of health-maintenance teaching rather than being discouraged.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → health maintenance → Breast health

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → health maintenance → Breast health (monthly self-examination); PDF p. 118 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Monthly breast self-exam angle distinct from mammography screening combo (cctc-1020) and skin-cancer teaching (cctc-1102); anchor verified on Cupples p. 118.

stem: A male transplant recipient asks about prostate health maintenance. Which screening practice aligns with standard references?

options.text: Prostate screening only after twenty years post-transplant
No prostate screening because immunosuppression prevents prostate disease
Monthly prostate biopsy for all recipients

explanation.rationale_correct: Prostate health maintenance includes annual prostate screening antigen testing, with urology consultation for urinary obstruction or recurrent urinary tract infection symptoms.

rationale_incorrect.B: Annual rather than exclusively late post-transplant screening is referenced.
rationale_incorrect.C: Immunosuppressed recipients still require age-appropriate prostate health maintenance.
rationale_incorrect.D: Annual PSA screening is referenced rather than routine monthly biopsy.

stem: When teaching testicular health maintenance after transplantation, which self-care practice aligns with standard references?

options.text: Testicular examination only once at transplant discharge
No testicular self-examination because immunosuppression prevents testicular cancer
Annual testicular biopsy for every recipient

explanation.rationale_correct: Testicular health teaching includes monthly self-examination as part of long-term health maintenance.

rationale_incorrect.B: Monthly rather than one-time self-examination is recommended.
rationale_incorrect.C: Immunosuppressed recipients still benefit from routine testicular self-examination teaching.
rationale_incorrect.D: Monthly self-examination is referenced rather than routine annual biopsy.

stem: A coordinator is updating gender-specific health-maintenance teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Monthly breast self-examination is recommended for breast health maintenance.
Annual prostate-specific antigen screening is part of prostate health maintenance.
Testicular health maintenance requires no self-examination because immunosuppression prevents cancer.
Papanicolaou testing includes regular assessment by a gynecologist.

explanation.rationale_correct: Monthly breast self-examination, annual PSA screening, and regular gynecologic Papanicolaou assessment are recommended. Statement III is false because testicular health teaching includes monthly self-examination.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—Papanicolaou testing includes regular gynecologic assessment.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false because monthly testicular self-examination is recommended.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Monthly self-examination … Annual prostate screening antigen … Testicular health … Papanicolaou test: Regular assessment by gynecologist
